title: Milestone 13: MagicaVoxel look (.vox, DDA voxel grid, sun/sky, bloom, style voxel)
abstract:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"adriendjn"} -->
_Requested by **Adrien** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FDRReMmT65iKMpjZABM1ZS?thread=cmsg_01FDRReMmT65iKMpjZABM1ZSFgJa5Yg6wRB3ydk5RwkuhA)_

Before: mypbr could not read MagicaVoxel models, had no sun, procedural sky, infinite ground or lens effects, and getting a voxel-art look took hand-built boxes.

After: `vox model.vox` loads MagicaVoxel files (palette, MATL materials, scene graph) and traces them with a 3D DDA voxel grid, and `style voxel` gives MagicaVoxel's look in one line. Classic scenes render as before unless they ask for the new features.

The work follows the steps in the "Making mypbr look like MagicaVoxel" analysis, one commit per step:

1. `.vox` loader, first as quad faces in the BVH (kept as `vox ... quads`).
2. `sun` (cone light given by irradiance), `sky uniform`, `ground` (infinite plane beside the BVH).
3. `bloom`, `vignette` (display images only) and polygonal bokeh with `camera blades`.
4. `voxel_grid`: Amanatides-Woo DDA in 8³ blocks inside a BVH. `voxel_test` checks it finds exactly the hits of the quads (200k random rays, 3 block sizes). About 15% faster than quads on monu1, and one byte per voxel.
5. `sky atmosphere`: single-scattering Rayleigh + Mie + ozone baked into an `environment_light`; the sun is reddened by the air.
6. `camera ortho`, `height_fog` (closed-form free-flight sampling), `bounces` caps, `transparent_shadows`, voxel `edges`.
7. `style voxel` / `style classic` preset; CLAUDE.md and ROADMAP.md updated.

How: everything is in headers under `include/` (`vox_loader.h`, `voxel.h`, `sun.h`, `plane.h`, `atmosphere.h`, `postprocess.h`), with scene keywords documented at the top of `scene.h`. `bounces` and `transparent_shadows` are deliberate MagicaVoxel-style biases, off unless set or `style voxel`. Test models: `scenes/models/island.vox` (generated by `tools/make_island_vox.py`) and ephtracy's MIT sample models via `tools/fetch_models.sh`. Renders: `renders/13-*.png`. Rebased on the Mitsuba validation merge; build warning-free, 4/4 tests pass.
